content.title: About
content.content: Multigrain crackers are crunchy biscuits made from a blend of whole grains, seeds, and sometimes nuts. They have a rich nutty‑grain flavor with a light salty note and work well as a snack on their own or as a base for toppings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Typical grain mix includes wheat, oats, rye, barley and sunflower seeds.
Multigrain crackers often contain more dietary fiber than white bread.
Flavor variations range from flaxseed and pumpkin seed to dried tomato and herb blends.
They are popular in diet plans because they pair easily with low‑calorie spreads.
In many countries they are served with cheese and ham as a classic appetizer.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: The whole‑grain blend provides dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs release energy slowly, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: B‑vitamin source
items.content: Grains supply thiamine, niacin and folate, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Seeds such as sunflower and flax add polyunsaturated fatty acids beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Crackers provide magnesium, iron and zinc, supporting muscle function and immunity.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Most crackers contain wheat, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some varieties are heavily salted; those monitoring sodium should choose low‑salt options.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Although light, crackers still contribute calories; moderation is key for weight management.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Flavored versions may contain sugar or honey, which can be problematic for diabetics.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy crackers straight from the pack, spread with cottage cheese, hummus, avocado, or use as a base for canapés with cheese and vegetables. They also add a pleasant crunch when tossed into soups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep crackers in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent mold.
